items.text: CRITICAL FINDING: The webhook handler for checkout.session.completed marks checkout_sessions.status = 'complete' BEFORE calling insertOrUpdateSubscription(), and these are NOT in the same DB transaction. If the subscription insert fails, the user has paid but gets no subscription — and nothing detects this state. This is the #1 reconciliation priority.

The codebase already has an anomaly tracking pattern: intro_anomaly_log table (main.go:1007-1018) with email, customer_id, anomaly_type, details JSONB, and indexes on email/type/created_at. This can be generalized into a payment_anomaly_log table covering all guardrail-detected anomalies.

269+ structured log events are emitted to stdout as JSON via logStructured()/logStructuredError(). All critical payment paths are already instrumented. The gap is consumption: no aggregation, alerting, or dashboards read these logs.

Credit consumption (ConsumeCreditsIdempotent) is fully atomic with BEGIN/COMMIT and FOR UPDATE locking. However, credit reversal is ad-hoc — only the AI gateway has an estimate-refund path. No generalized credit adjustment endpoint exists for customer support.

Admin endpoints are extensive (coupons, downloads, bundles, users, Stripe settings) but have zero payment operations: no customer payment lookup, no entitlement grant/revoke, no credit adjustment, no stuck-session viewer, no manual reconciliation trigger.

items.context: The reconciliation job needs to run periodically. LPBS currently has no cron/scheduler infrastructure. Options range from a simple goroutine ticker inside the API process to an external scheduler.

options.label: In-process goroutine ticker — API starts a background goroutine on boot that runs reconciliation every N minutes
options.rationale: Simplest to implement, no external dependencies, shuts down with the API. Risk: if the API crashes, reconciliation stops too — but that's acceptable since a crashed API has bigger problems.

options.label: Separate reconciliation CLI command — a `reconcile` subcommand that can be invoked by cron or the scenario lifecycle
options.rationale: Decoupled from API uptime, can run independently. Adds a new binary entry point and scheduling complexity.

items.context: When the in-app anomaly detection fires, how should the operator be notified? This affects implementation complexity and whether alerts are seen promptly.

options.label: Admin dashboard polling — anomalies written to DB, admin panel shows a badge/count, operator checks periodically
options.rationale: Simplest implementation, no external notification service needed. Risk: operator may not check frequently enough.

options.label: Webhook callback — POST anomaly details to a configurable URL (e.g., Slack incoming webhook, Discord, or a monitoring endpoint)
options.rationale: Near-real-time notification, integrates with existing alerting tools. Moderate complexity — needs a configurable URL and retry logic.

options.label: Email alerts — send email via existing SMTP/SendGrid integration when anomaly thresholds are breached
options.rationale: Familiar notification channel, but requires email service configuration and may have delivery delays.
